newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL interbank rates steady in thin trading.
newsitem.headline: KL interbank rates steady in thin trading.

text.p: Interbank rates remained stable in thin activity as lenders were wary of lending any lower amid persistent rumours of a new long-term government bond issue, dealers said.
Speculation has been rife that the central Bank Negara will announce a new Malaysian Government Securities (MGS) issue to roll over maturing bonds.
A 900-million ringgit long-term government bond issue will mature on May 15.
"The market will be more cautious as it gets closer to May 15. So far rates have been holding steady," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank.

Dealers said a new Bank Negara bill issue would slow down pressure on short-term rates. The Bank will issue Bank Negara bills worth 500 million ringgit on Wednesday, matching the 500-million ringgit bill issue which matured last Friday.
One-week money was at 6.9/7.0 percent against 7.00/10 on Friday, while two-week and three-week were quoted around Friday's 7.10/20 and 7.20/30 percent respectively.
One-month money at 7.25/30 percent, three-month at 7.35/40 and six-month at 7.40/45, were all unchanged.
The overnight interbank rate is expected to hover around 6.0 percent after closing at 5.9/6.0 percent on Friday.
Dealers said Bank Negara was likely to support the overnight rate from falling below its perceived floor of 5.80 percent.
